methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a seed-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The relevant peer universe consists of 7 private companies operating in this space, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this narrow subsector.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient clustering of comparable companies at matching stage and valuation tiers. Of the 5 same-sector peers identified, none met the filters for same-stage or adjacent-stage positioning, and no three or more peers aligned on similar valuation tier. A broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models and capital intensity within Drones & Autonomous. Consequently, no triangulated valuation range can be supported by the available data.

Without sufficient comparable transactions, revenue multiples, or founder-stage pricing precedents in this subsector, further valuation work would require either: (1) collection of transaction data from the identified peer set if available; (2) stage-agnostic benchmarking against the full 7-company private peer set with explicit disclosure of methodological limitations; or (3) alternative approaches such as DCF or venture capital method inputs. The scarcity of seed-stage drones companies with public pricing suggests this market segment remains nascent and illiquid for valuation anchoring purposes.
